library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Carreno_2026_belantamab_kva"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70276> (open access)
* Supplement: Methods S1, Tables S1-S12, Figures S1-S6; File S1 (example
  simulation dataset) and File S2 (the authors' mrgsolve simulation code).

Carreno 2026 builds a simulation framework for belantamab mafodotin, an
anti-BCMA antibody-drug conjugate, given with bortezomib + dexamethasone (BVd),
pomalidomide + dexamethasone (BPd) or lenalidomide + dexamethasone (BRd) in
relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. The framework (Figure 1A) joins three
separately estimated models, all driven by the belantamab mafodotin
concentration from the Papathanasiou 2025 population PK model:

1. a serum **M-protein tumor growth inhibition model** fitted to BVd data
   (DREAMM-6 Arm B and DREAMM-7), packaged as
   `Carreno_2026_belantamab_mprotein_bvd`;
2. the same structure re-estimated on BPd data (DREAMM-8), packaged as
   `Carreno_2026_belantamab_mprotein_bpd`;
3. a **continuous-time Markov model (CTMM)** of ophthalmic exam finding (OEF)
   grades on the Keratopathy and Visual Acuity (KVA) scale, fitted to
   monotherapy and combination data from five studies, packaged as
   `Carreno_2026_belantamab_kva`.

Each model file carries its own copy of the PK driver, so each can be solved on
its own. The framework's dose holds, dose reductions, schedule extensions and
dropouts are simulation rules, not model equations; they are reproduced below
as an R harness around the packaged models.

```{r models}
mod_bvd <- readModelDb("Carreno_2026_belantamab_mprotein_bvd")
mod_bpd <- readModelDb("Carreno_2026_belantamab_mprotein_bpd")
mod_kva <- readModelDb("Carreno_2026_belantamab_kva")
```

# Population

| | BVd M-protein model | BPd M-protein model | KVA model |
|---|---|---|---|
| Studies | DREAMM-6 Arm B, DREAMM-7 | DREAMM-8 | DREAMM-2, -3, -6, -7, -8 |
| Patients (observations) | 260 (4829) | 103 (1173) | 959 (15,374) |
| Female | 45% | 34% | 42% |
| Age, median (range), years | 65 (32-86) | 67 (40-82) | 66 (32-89) |
| Weight, median (range), kg | 74.7 (43.7-133) | 77.5 (46.0-117) | 75.2 (37.0-170) |
| Albumin, median, g/L | 40.0 | 41.0 | 40.0 |
| sBCMA, median (range), ug/L | 40.2 (2.20-729) | 40.0 (0.975-741) | 49.7 (0.975-2026) |
| IgG, median (range), g/L | 20.3 (1.05-81.5) | 18.0 (0.800-96.3) | 13.6 (0.350-106) |
| M-protein, median (range), g/L | 19.0 (5.00-85.0) | 17.5 (5.30-83.7) | not reported |

Source: Carreno 2026 Table 1 and Table S2. M-protein models included patients
with baseline serum M-protein >= 5 g/L and at least one post-baseline value.
The KVA model imputed grade 0 when no OEF was present; observed grades were
0 (17%), 1 (15%), 2 (36%), 3 (30%) and 4 (2%), with grades 3 and 4 combined in
the model.

# Model structure

**PK driver (all three files).** Two-compartment model with sigmoid
time-varying clearance,
CL(t) = CL0 * exp(Imax * t^gamma / (TI50^gamma + t^gamma)), and the
Papathanasiou 2025 covariates (weight, albumin, sBCMA, IgG, BMI, race,
combination therapy). The values are those printed in File S2.

**M-protein (BVd and BPd).** From File S2 `$DES`:

dM/dt = KGR * (1 - M/150) * M/(M + A50) * M - KDEATH * (1 - exp(-S * C)) * R * M,

with R = exp(-LAM * t) (resistance), C the central belantamab mafodotin
concentration (ug/mL) and M(0) the baseline M-protein floored at 5 g/L. In the
BVd model log KDEATH is shifted by -0.0884 * (log(IgG) - 2.74).

**KVA CTMM.** Four states (grade 0, 1, 2, 3/4) holding occupancy probabilities.
With Cn = C / 3.357 ug/mL:

* upward rates 0->1, 0->2, 2->3/4: GNu * Cn^GMu; 1->2 adds
  GNu12 * Cn^GMu12 in DREAMM-6;
* downward rates i->j: Kij * GNd / (1 + GNd * Cn^GMd), with K20 = K21.

Vd, Rd and Pd modify K10, K21, GNu, GMu and GNd (Table S6, Table S7), and
baseline sBCMA scales GNu.

# Typical-patient predictions

The typical patient below has the Table 1 BVd medians (75 kg, albumin 40 g/L,
sBCMA 40 ug/L, IgG 20 g/L, baseline M-protein 19 g/L, BMI 27 kg/m^2). Doses
are 30-minute infusions in mg (mg/kg x weight), as in File S1.

```{r typical-cov}
typ <- data.frame(
  WT = 75, ALB = 40, SBCMA = 40, IGG = 20, BMI = 27, MCPROT = 19,
  RACE_ASIAN = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0, COMBO_BELAMAF = 1,
  COMBO_BOR_DEX = 0, COMBO_LEN_DEX = 0, COMBO_POM_DEX = 0, STUDY_DREAMM6 = 0
)
dose_events <- function(times, mgkg, wt) {
  data.frame(time = times, evid = 1L, amt = mgkg * wt, dur = 0.5 / 24, cmt = "central")
}
```

## M-protein under protocol dosing without modification

DREAMM-7 protocol dosing is 2.5 mg/kg Q3W; DREAMM-8 is 2.5 mg/kg in Cycle 1 and
1.9 mg/kg Q4W thereafter (Table S1). Without dose holds the typical patient's
M-protein falls by well over 90% (VGPR) in both regimens.

```{r typical-mprotein}
t_obs <- seq(0, 2 * 365, by = 3)
ev_bvd <- bind_rows(
  dose_events(seq(0, by = 21, length.out = 35), 2.5, 75),
  data.frame(time = t_obs, evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "mprotein")
) |>
  mutate(id = 1L) |>
  cbind(typ)
ev_bpd <- bind_rows(
  dose_events(0, 2.5, 75),
  dose_events(seq(28, by = 28, length.out = 25), 1.9, 75),
  data.frame(time = t_obs, evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "mprotein")
) |>
  mutate(id = 1L) |>
  cbind(typ)

typ_mp <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(rxSolve(zeroRe(mod_bvd), ev_bvd, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    mutate(model = "BVd model, 2.5 mg/kg Q3W"),
  as.data.frame(rxSolve(zeroRe(mod_bpd), ev_bpd, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    mutate(model = "BPd model, 2.5 then 1.9 mg/kg Q4W")
)

ggplot(typ_mp, aes(time / 30.4375, mprotein, colour = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.1 * 19, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time (months)", y = "Serum M-protein (g/L)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Dashed line: 90% reduction from baseline (VGPR threshold).") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r typical-mprotein-check}
red_12m <- typ_mp |>
  filter(time == 366) |>
  mutate(reduction = 1 - mprotein / 19)
red_12m[, c("model", "mprotein", "reduction")]
stopifnot(all(red_12m$reduction > 0.9))
```

## KVA grade probabilities by backbone

Carreno 2026 Table S7 lists how the comedication factors move each CTMM
parameter. The chunk below checks the packaged model against that table at
`SBCMA = 50` (the reference), then shows the typical grade-probability time
course under uninterrupted 2.5 mg/kg Q3W dosing.

```{r table-s7}
backbones <- tibble::tribble(
  ~backbone,     ~COMBO_BELAMAF, ~COMBO_BOR_DEX, ~COMBO_LEN_DEX, ~COMBO_POM_DEX,
  "Monotherapy", 0,              0,              0,              0,
  "Vd",          1,              1,              0,              0,
  "Rd",          1,              0,              1,              0,
  "Pd",          1,              0,              0,              1
)
ev_s7 <- backbones |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), time = 1, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L,
         WT = 75, ALB = 40, SBCMA = 50, IGG = 15, BMI = 27,
         RACE_ASIAN = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0, STUDY_DREAMM6 = 0)
s7 <- rxSolve(mod_kva, ev_s7, omega = NA, sigma = NA, returnType = "data.frame",
              keep = "backbone")
s7 <- s7 |>
  transmute(backbone, K10 = lambda10, K21 = lambda21, K32 = lambda32,
            GNu = gnu, GMu = gmu_i, GNd = gnd)
paper_s7 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~backbone,     ~K10,     ~K21,     ~K32,    ~GNu,    ~GMu,   ~GNd,
  "Monotherapy", 0.02806,  0.009361, 0.03338, 0.02145, 0.1549, 3.908,
  "Vd",          0.007061, 0.009361, 0.03338, 0.02905, 0.2052, 3.994,
  "Rd",          0.02806,  0.005837, 0.03338, 0.02905, 0.5229, 3.908,
  "Pd",          0.007061, 0.009361, 0.03338, 0.02905, 0.2052, 3.994
)
knitr::kable(s7, digits = 5, caption = "Packaged model, reference sBCMA (compare Carreno 2026 Table S7).")
rel_err <- abs(as.matrix(s7[, -1]) / as.matrix(paper_s7[, -1]) - 1)
stopifnot(max(rel_err) < 1e-3)
```

The Table S7 values agree to within rounding of the printed four significant
figures.

```{r typical-kva}
ev_kva <- bind_rows(
  dose_events(seq(0, by = 21, length.out = 18), 2.5, 75),
  data.frame(time = seq(0, 365, by = 1), evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0,
             cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
)
kva_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(backbones)), function(i) {
  ev <- ev_kva |> mutate(id = 1L) |> cbind(typ[, setdiff(names(typ), names(backbones))]) |>
    cbind(backbones[i, -1])
  rxSolve(zeroRe(mod_kva), ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(backbone = backbones$backbone[i])
}))
prob_sum <- with(kva_typ, s_kva0 + s_kva1 + s_kva2 + s_kva34)
stopifnot(max(abs(prob_sum - 1)) < 1e-6)

kva_typ |>
  select(time, backbone, `Grade 0` = p_kva0, `Grade 1` = p_kva1,
         `Grade 2` = p_kva2, `Grade 3/4` = p_kva34) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("Grade"), names_to = "grade", values_to = "p") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 30.4375, p, fill = grade)) +
  geom_area() +
  facet_wrap(~backbone) +
  labs(x = "Time (months)", y = "Probability", fill = "KVA grade",
       caption = "Typical patient, 2.5 mg/kg Q3W without dose holds.") +
  theme_bw()
```

The four occupancy probabilities sum to 1 throughout (checked above). Without
dose holds, grade 3/4 becomes the most likely state within a few months.

## Transition rates against concentration

Figure 2 of Carreno 2026 shows that the probability of moving to a higher grade
rises with concentration, and the probability of moving down falls. The chunk
below plots the model's instantaneous rates for a typical BVd patient.

```{r rates-conc}
conc <- c(0, exp(seq(log(0.01), log(40), length.out = 200)))
pars <- as.list(rxode2::rxode2(mod_kva)$theta)
cn <- conc / pars$cref_kva
gnu <- exp(pars$lgnu) * pars$e_combo_gnu * (40 / 50)^pars$e_sbcma_gnu
gmu <- pars$gmu * pars$e_bor_gmu
gnd <- exp(pars$lgnd) * pars$e_bor_gnd
rates <- tibble::tibble(
  conc = conc,
  `up (0->1, 1->2, 2->3/4)` = gnu * cn^gmu,
  `down 1->0` = exp(pars$llambda10) * pars$e_bor_lambda10 * gnd / (1 + gnd * cn^pars$gmd),
  `down 2->1` = exp(pars$llambda21) * gnd / (1 + gnd * cn^pars$gmd),
  `down 3/4->2` = exp(pars$llambda32) * gnd / (1 + gnd * cn^pars$gmd)
)
rates |>
  filter(conc > 0) |>
  pivot_longer(-conc, names_to = "transition", values_to = "rate") |>
  ggplot(aes(conc, rate, colour = transition)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Belantamab mafodotin concentration (ug/mL)", y = "Transition rate (1/day)",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Framework simulation

## Harness

The harness follows File S2. Each patient is assessed once per cycle (21 days
for BVd, 28 days for BPd). At every assessment the KVA grade is drawn from the
CTMM probabilities and the Markov states are reset to that grade (the code's
`EVID = 3` reset). A dose is held while the grade is >= 2; once a scheduled dose
has been missed, dosing resumes at grade <= 1 at the reduced level and
interval. Belantamab mafodotin amounts in the PK compartments are carried
across cycles with replacement events (`evid = 5`), which reproduces an
uninterrupted solve exactly.

The M-protein model does not affect dosing, so it is solved afterwards on each
patient's realised dosing history. Progression is defined per IMWG as an
increase of > 25% over the lowest M-protein to date with an absolute increase
of > 5 g/L. Dropout for other reasons is drawn from the Methods S1 log-normal
models. Outcomes are counted up to the first of progression, other dropout or
50 months.

Virtual cohorts of 200 patients take covariates from log-normal distributions
matched to the Table 1 medians and ranges, and random effects drawn from the
packaged IIV. All random numbers come from base R with a fixed seed, so the
cohort is the same on every machine.

```{r harness}
rlnorm_range <- function(n, med, lo, hi) {
  pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(med), (log(hi) - log(lo)) / 6)), lo), hi)
}

make_cohort <- function(n, tab) {
  data.frame(
    id = seq_len(n),
    WT = rlnorm_range(n, tab$wt[1], tab$wt[2], tab$wt[3]),
    ALB = rlnorm_range(n, tab$alb[1], tab$alb[2], tab$alb[3]),
    SBCMA = rlnorm_range(n, tab$sbcma[1], tab$sbcma[2], tab$sbcma[3]),
    IGG = rlnorm_range(n, tab$igg[1], tab$igg[2], tab$igg[3]),
    MCPROT = rlnorm_range(n, tab$mprot[1], tab$mprot[2], tab$mprot[3]),
    BMI = 27, RACE_ASIAN = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0, COMBO_BELAMAF = 1,
    COMBO_BOR_DEX = tab$bor, COMBO_LEN_DEX = 0, COMBO_POM_DEX = tab$pom,
    STUDY_DREAMM6 = 0
  )
}

draw_eta <- function(mod, n) {
  om <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$omega
  e <- matrix(rnorm(n * nrow(om)), n) %*% chol(om)
  colnames(e) <- rownames(om)
  as.data.frame(e)
}

kva_cols <- c("id", "WT", "ALB", "SBCMA", "IGG", "BMI", "RACE_ASIAN", "RACE_BLACK",
              "COMBO_BELAMAF", "COMBO_BOR_DEX", "COMBO_LEN_DEX", "COMBO_POM_DEX",
              "STUDY_DREAMM6")

# One cycle for every patient: replace the PK amounts carried from the previous
# cycle, reset the grade probabilities to the grade just drawn, give the
# cycle's dose, and observe at the start of the next cycle.
solve_cycle <- function(state, tc, len, amt, eta) {
  base <- cbind(state[, kva_cols], eta)
  rep_rows <- function(cmt, val) {
    mutate(base, time = tc, evid = 5L, cmt = cmt, amt = val, dur = 0, dvid = NA_integer_)
  }
  g <- state$grade
  ev <- bind_rows(
    rep_rows("central", state$central),
    rep_rows("peripheral1", state$peripheral1),
    rep_rows("s_kva0", as.numeric(g == 0)),
    rep_rows("s_kva1", as.numeric(g == 1)),
    rep_rows("s_kva2", as.numeric(g == 2)),
    rep_rows("s_kva34", as.numeric(g == 3)),
    mutate(base, time = tc, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", amt = amt, dur = 0.5 / 24,
           dvid = NA_integer_)[amt > 0, ],
    mutate(base, time = tc + len, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0, dur = 0, dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid == 5L))
  rxSolve(mod_kva, ev, omega = NA, sigma = NA, returnType = "data.frame")
}

run_kva_harness <- function(cohort, eta, sched, n_cycles) {
  n <- nrow(cohort)
  state <- cohort
  state$central <- 0
  state$peripheral1 <- 0
  state$grade <- 0L
  tdose <- rep(-Inf, n)
  reduced <- rep(FALSE, n)
  grades <- matrix(NA_integer_, n, n_cycles)
  doses <- matrix(0, n, n_cycles)
  for (cyc in seq_len(n_cycles)) {
    tc <- (cyc - 1) * sched$len
    hold <- state$grade >= sched$hold_grade
    interval <- ifelse(reduced, sched$int2, sched$int1)
    due <- (tc - tdose) >= interval - 1e-6
    give <- due & !hold
    level <- ifelse(reduced, sched$red_level, sched$level(cyc))
    amt <- ifelse(give, level * cohort$WT, 0)
    reduced <- reduced | (due & hold)
    tdose[give] <- tc
    doses[, cyc] <- amt
    grades[, cyc] <- state$grade
    s <- solve_cycle(state, tc, sched$len, amt, eta)
    p <- as.matrix(s[, c("p_kva0", "p_kva1", "p_kva2", "p_kva34")])
    u <- runif(n)
    state$grade <- pmin(as.integer(rowSums(u > t(apply(p, 1, cumsum)))), 3L)
    state$central <- s$central
    state$peripheral1 <- s$peripheral1
  }
  list(grades = grades, doses = doses)
}

solve_mprotein <- function(mod, cohort, eta, doses, len) {
  n_cyc <- ncol(doses)
  tc <- (seq_len(n_cyc) - 1) * len
  cov <- cbind(cohort, eta)
  dose_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_cyc), function(cyc) {
    keep <- doses[, cyc] > 0
    if (!any(keep)) return(NULL)
    mutate(cov[keep, , drop = FALSE], time = tc[cyc], amt = doses[keep, cyc])
  })) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dur = 0.5 / 24)
  obs_ev <- cov[rep(seq_len(nrow(cov)), each = n_cyc), ] |>
    mutate(time = rep(tc, nrow(cov)), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "mprotein", dur = 0)
  ev <- bind_rows(dose_ev, obs_ev) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
  s <- rxSolve(mod, ev, omega = NA, sigma = NA, returnType = "data.frame")
  matrix(s$mprotein, nrow = nrow(cohort), byrow = TRUE)
}

summarise_outcomes <- function(mp, grades, len, meanlog, sdlog, months = 50) {
  n <- nrow(mp)
  n_cyc <- ncol(mp)
  tc <- (seq_len(n_cyc) - 1) * len
  t_end <- months * 30.4375
  base <- mp[, 1]
  t_pd <- rep(Inf, n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    nadir <- base[i]
    for (cyc in 2:n_cyc) {
      if (mp[i, cyc] > 1.25 * nadir && mp[i, cyc] - nadir > 5) {
        t_pd[i] <- tc[cyc]
        break
      }
      nadir <- min(nadir, mp[i, cyc])
    }
  }
  t_other <- rlnorm(n, meanlog, sdlog)
  t_cens <- pmin(t_pd, t_other, t_end)
  seen <- outer(rep(1, n), tc) <= t_cens
  red <- 1 - mp / base
  pfs_time <- t_cens / 30.4375
  pfs_event <- t_pd <= pmin(t_other, t_end)
  km <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(pfs_time, pfs_event) ~ 1)
  ks <- summary(km, times = c(12, 24), extend = TRUE)$surv
  list(
    summary = data.frame(
      ORR = 100 * mean(rowSums(seen & red >= 0.5) > 0),
      VGPR = 100 * mean(rowSums(seen & red >= 0.9) > 0),
      PFS12 = 100 * ks[1],
      PFS24 = 100 * ks[2],
      mPFS = unname(summary(km)$table["median"]),
      G2 = 100 * mean(rowSums(seen & grades >= 2) > 0),
      G3 = 100 * mean(rowSums(seen & grades >= 3) > 0)
    ),
    km = data.frame(time = km$time, surv = km$surv)
  )
}
```

## BVd: DREAMM-7 reference and an extended schedule

Table 2 of Carreno 2026 simulates BVd regimens over 50 months with holds for
grade >= 2 and restart at grade <= 1. The reference is 2.5 mg/kg Q3W with
restart at 1.9 mg/kg Q3W; the extended schedule is 2.5 mg/kg Q6W with restart at
1.9 mg/kg Q6W. Both arms share the same virtual patients.

```{r sim-bvd}
set.seed(20261113)
n_pat <- 200
cohort_bvd <- make_cohort(n_pat, list(
  wt = c(74.7, 43.7, 133), alb = c(40, 23, 51), sbcma = c(40.2, 2.2, 729),
  igg = c(20.3, 1.05, 81.5), mprot = c(19, 5, 85), bor = 1, pom = 0
))
eta_kva <- draw_eta(mod_kva, n_pat)
eta_pk <- eta_kva[, c("etalcl", "etalvc", "etalq", "etalvp", "etacl_time_max", "etalcl_t50")]
mp_names <- c("etalkg", "etalkd", "etallambda", "etalslope", "etala50")
eta_mp_bvd <- draw_eta(mod_bvd, n_pat)[, mp_names]

n_cyc_bvd <- ceiling(50 * 30.4375 / 21)
sched_ref <- list(len = 21, int1 = 21, int2 = 21, hold_grade = 2, red_level = 1.9,
                  level = function(cyc) 2.5)
sched_q6w <- list(len = 21, int1 = 42, int2 = 42, hold_grade = 2, red_level = 1.9,
                  level = function(cyc) 2.5)

h_ref <- run_kva_harness(cohort_bvd, eta_kva, sched_ref, n_cyc_bvd)
h_q6w <- run_kva_harness(cohort_bvd, eta_kva, sched_q6w, n_cyc_bvd)
mp_ref <- solve_mprotein(mod_bvd, cohort_bvd, cbind(eta_pk, eta_mp_bvd), h_ref$doses, 21)
mp_q6w <- solve_mprotein(mod_bvd, cohort_bvd, cbind(eta_pk, eta_mp_bvd), h_q6w$doses, 21)
out_ref <- summarise_outcomes(mp_ref, h_ref$grades, 21, 8.209, 2.656)
out_q6w <- summarise_outcomes(mp_q6w, h_q6w$grades, 21, 8.209, 2.656)
```

```{r bvd-table}
paper_t2 <- data.frame(
  ORR = c(91.0, 90.0), VGPR = c(61.5, 55.0), PFS12 = c(80.3, 76.3),
  PFS24 = c(65.7, 59.8), mPFS = c(37.3, 31.1), G2 = c(97.0, 92.5), G3 = c(85.5, 77.5)
)
sim_t2 <- bind_rows(out_ref$summary, out_q6w$summary)
bvd_cmp <- bind_rows(
  mutate(sim_t2, Source = "Simulated (this vignette)"),
  mutate(paper_t2, Source = "Carreno 2026 Table 2")
) |>
  mutate(Regimen = rep(c("2.5 mg/kg Q3W (reference)", "2.5 mg/kg Q6W"), 2)) |>
  arrange(Regimen, Source) |>
  select(Regimen, Source, everything()) |>
  rename(`ORR (%)` = ORR, `VGPR+ (%)` = VGPR, `PFS 12 mo (%)` = PFS12,
         `PFS 24 mo (%)` = PFS24, `mPFS (mo)` = mPFS,
         `Grade >= 2 KVA (%)` = G2, `Grade >= 3 KVA (%)` = G3)
knitr::kable(bvd_cmp, digits = 1)
```

```{r bvd-km}
bind_rows(
  mutate(out_ref$km, regimen = "2.5 mg/kg Q3W (reference)"),
  mutate(out_q6w$km, regimen = "2.5 mg/kg Q6W")
) |>
  bind_rows(data.frame(time = 0, surv = 1, regimen = c("2.5 mg/kg Q3W (reference)", "2.5 mg/kg Q6W"))) |>
  arrange(regimen, time) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, surv, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_step() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 50), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Time (months)", y = "Progression-free (progression only)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Compare Carreno 2026 Figure 3 (simulated BVd PFS).") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## BPd: DREAMM-8 reference

The BPd reference (Table S8) is 2.5 mg/kg in Cycle 1 then 1.9 mg/kg Q4W, held
for grade >= 2 and restarted at 1.9 mg/kg Q8W.

```{r sim-bpd}
cohort_bpd <- make_cohort(n_pat, list(
  wt = c(77.5, 46, 117), alb = c(41, 25, 49), sbcma = c(40, 0.975, 741),
  igg = c(18, 0.8, 96.3), mprot = c(17.5, 5.3, 83.7), bor = 0, pom = 1
))
eta_mp_bpd <- draw_eta(mod_bpd, n_pat)[, mp_names]
sched_bpd <- list(len = 28, int1 = 28, int2 = 56, hold_grade = 2, red_level = 1.9,
                  level = function(cyc) ifelse(cyc == 1, 2.5, 1.9))
n_cyc_bpd <- ceiling(50 * 30.4375 / 28)
h_bpd <- run_kva_harness(cohort_bpd, eta_kva, sched_bpd, n_cyc_bpd)
mp_bpd <- solve_mprotein(mod_bpd, cohort_bpd, cbind(eta_pk, eta_mp_bpd), h_bpd$doses, 28)
out_bpd <- summarise_outcomes(mp_bpd, h_bpd$grades, 28, 9.296, 3.643)

paper_s8 <- data.frame(ORR = 87.4, VGPR = 60.2, PFS12 = 78.1, PFS24 = 66.4,
                       mPFS = NA_real_, G2 = 95.1, G3 = 78.6)
bind_rows(
  mutate(out_bpd$summary, Source = "Simulated (this vignette)"),
  mutate(paper_s8, Source = "Carreno 2026 Table S8")
) |>
  select(Source, everything()) |>
  rename(`ORR (%)` = ORR, `VGPR+ (%)` = VGPR, `PFS 12 mo (%)` = PFS12,
         `PFS 24 mo (%)` = PFS24, `mPFS (mo)` = mPFS,
         `Grade >= 2 KVA (%)` = G2, `Grade >= 3 KVA (%)` = G3) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "mPFS was not reached in Table S8 (NA).")
```

## Agreement with the published framework

```{r framework-check}
sim_all <- bind_rows(out_ref$summary, out_q6w$summary, out_bpd$summary)
pub_all <- bind_rows(paper_t2, paper_s8)
diff_pts <- sim_all[, c("VGPR", "G2", "G3")] - pub_all[, c("VGPR", "G2", "G3")]
diff_pts
stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed kill, growth or transition parameter moves these by
  # tens of percentage points; the cohort is drawn with base R and a fixed seed.
  all(abs(as.matrix(diff_pts)) < 15),
  # Extending the BVd schedule must not increase grade >= 3 incidence.
  out_q6w$summary$G3 <= out_ref$summary$G3 + 5
)
```

Across the three regimens the simulated VGPR+ rates and grade >= 2 and >= 3
KVA incidences fall within
`r round(max(abs(as.matrix(diff_pts))), 1)` percentage points of the published
framework. The regimen ordering is preserved: the Q6W schedule gives a shorter
median PFS (`r round(out_q6w$summary$mPFS, 1)` against
`r round(out_ref$summary$mPFS, 1)` months; published 31.1 against 37.3) and no
more grade >= 3 findings than Q3W.

The simulated BVd overall response rate
(`r round(out_ref$summary$ORR, 1)`% against 91.0%) and the BVd PFS
landmarks are lower than in Table 2. The likely reason is that Carreno 2026
simulated the DREAMM-7 patients with their individual post hoc random effects,
which shrink toward the typical value. This vignette draws from the full
estimated between-subject variance (omega KGR = 1.65), which gives more
fast-growing, non-responding patients. The BPd simulation, with smaller
M-protein variances, lands closer to Table S8.

# PK driver: cycle 1 NCA

The PK driver is used unchanged from Papathanasiou 2025; Carreno 2026 reports
no PK summaries. For reference, the cycle 1 exposure of a typical patient after
2.5 mg/kg is computed with PKNCA, for monotherapy and for combination therapy.
Combination therapy changes only the time-varying part of clearance, so cycle 1
exposure differs little.

```{r pknca}
t_nca <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 21, by = 0.25), 0.5 / 24)))
nca_in <- bind_rows(lapply(c(0, 1), function(combo) {
  ev <- bind_rows(
    dose_events(0, 2.5, 75),
    data.frame(time = t_nca, evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "mprotein")
  ) |>
    mutate(id = 1L) |>
    cbind(typ |> mutate(COMBO_BELAMAF = combo))
  rxSolve(zeroRe(mod_bvd), ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(id = combo + 1L, treatment = ifelse(combo == 1, "Combination", "Monotherapy"))
}))
conc_df <- nca_in |> filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1:2, treatment = c("Monotherapy", "Combination"),
                      time = 0, amt = 2.5 * 75)
o_conc <- PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
o_data <- PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose,
                    intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 21, cmax = TRUE,
                                           tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE))
nca_res <- pk.nca(o_data)
as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  rename(Treatment = treatment, `Cmax (ug/mL)` = cmax, `Tmax (day)` = tmax,
         `AUC0-21 (ug*day/mL)` = auclast) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Model code outranks the table where they differ.** File S2 is the
  authors' implementation and is followed for structure:
  * The kill-term slope S (Table S4 "TVE50", 0.398 mL/ug) is a log-scale
    THETA in the code (`LNS = THETA69`, `S = exp(LNS + ETAS)`), so
    S = exp(0.398) = 1.49 mL/ug. The BPd value 0.432 is treated the same way.
  * The carrying capacity of 150 g/L, the 5 g/L floor on baseline M-protein,
    the KVA normalising concentration 3.357 ug/mL and the form
    K * GNd / (1 + GNd * Cn^GMd) of the downward rates are taken from the code.
    Table S4 and the main text do not print them.
  * The main text says both M-protein models include "a baseline elimination
    rate constant that occurs in the absence of belantamab mafodotin". The
    code has no such term (the kill term is zero without drug), and it is not
    included here.
  * Resistance is a state in the code, starting at 1 with d/dt = -LAM * state.
    It is written here in the identical closed form exp(-LAM * t).
* **M-protein proportional residual error.** Table S4 heads the row
  "Residual proportional error variance". The code holds it as a THETA next to
  the additive-SD THETA, in a combined W = sqrt(PROP^2 * IPRED^2 + ADD^2)
  form (commented `WBAS` line). The values 0.333 (BVd) and 0.414 (BPd) are
  therefore used as proportional SDs.
* **Table S4 covariance labels.** The fourth entry of each M-protein IIV block
  is labelled a second "Covariance (KGR~KDEATH)". In the NONMEM lower-triangle
  order the table follows, it is the KGR~LAM covariance, and it is encoded that
  way. Both blocks are positive definite.
* **BPd model structure.** File S2 implements the BVd model only. The paper
  states that the final BVd model was the base model for the BPd model, so the
  BPd file uses the same equations with the Table S4 BPd values and no IgG
  effect.
* **PK random effects and residual error.** Carreno 2026 used individual post
  hoc PK estimates and does not report the PK IIV or residual error. These
  values are taken from the Papathanasiou 2025 publication, as packaged in
  `Papathanasiou_2025_belantamab`. The PK fixed effects use the more precise
  values printed in File S2 (for example CL 0.925475 L/day against 0.926 in
  Papathanasiou 2025 Table 2).
* **Combination indicators in the KVA model.** File S2 applies the "D678"
  factor on GNu to the DREAMM-6, -7 and -8 studies, which are exactly the
  combination-therapy patients, so it is keyed to `COMBO_BELAMAF`. The Vd
  factors on K10, GMu and GNd apply to Vd and also to Pd (the paper set the Pd
  effects equal to Vd). The DREAMM-6 grade 1 to 2 effect is keyed to
  `STUDY_DREAMM6` (both arms), following the code's `DREAMM == 6` condition.
  Several DREAMM-7-only Vd factors (File S2 THETA37-THETA39, THETA42) and all
  Rd factors other than K21 and GMu equal 1, are absent from Table S6 and are
  omitted. The Table S6 footnote calls BOR_GMu an effect on the "downward"
  exponent, but the code and Table S7 apply it to the upward exponent GMu.
* **Imax on the linear scale.** The maximal log-fold change in clearance,
  `cl_time_max` (-0.403), is negative and carries an additive random effect
  (File S2: `IMAX = TVIMAX + ETAIMAX`), so it stays untransformed in `ini()`.
  The convention check's log-transform suggestion does not apply to it.
* **Baseline KVA grade.** File S2 starts each patient at the observed baseline
  grade (`BAS2`). The packaged model starts every patient at grade 0, since
  baseline keratopathy was present in only 1% of patients (Table S5). To start
  elsewhere, replace the `s_kva*` states with an `evid = 5` event at time 0.
* **Framework harness.** The harness is a simplification of the File S2 dosing
  logic. Once a scheduled dose has been missed, every later dose uses the
  reduced level and interval. Assessments fall at the start of each cycle
  rather than 2 hours before the dose. Death is not simulated, so PFS here
  counts progression only. Virtual covariates are drawn from Table 1 medians
  and ranges; BMI is fixed at 27 kg/m^2 and race at the non-Asian, non-Black
  reference, because Table 1 does not report them for these populations.
